text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The cabinet decided at its meeting yesterday to improve working methods in some sectors of the government bureaucracy, to make procedures easier for the public. Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif said the cabinet decided to develop the way people pay their telephone, water and electricity bills and the pensions department will open 4,759 outlets for disbursing pension payments.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri called for integration and cooperation between Arab countries in tourism. He was speaking at the inaugural meeting of the new council of Arab tourism ministers.

- Sultan Qaboos bin Said of Oman will visit Egypt for three days from Saturday and will have talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak. They will discuss Arab and regional developments, the challenges to the peace process and steps to set up an Arab common market.
- The administrative court overruled Health Minister Ismail Sallam's decree banning female circumcision.
- Sherif Raafat named head of the stock exchange.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said at the cabinet meeting that the government will pursue its efforts to eliminate all the problems the public faces in service sectors.
- The Damascus Declaration states will discuss an Arab common market in Latakia today.

- An official source at the Ministry of Finance said the total revenue collected from taxes, customs and sales this financial year up to the end of May was 35 billion pounds ($10.3 billion) or 87 percent (of the target for the whole year). The source was optimistic that the target could be met. The year ends on June 30.
- South African President Nelson Mandela will visit Egypt in September. Mandela announced the visit during a visit to the Egyptian embassy in South Africa.
- Public prrosecutor Raga el-Arabi has agreed to refer the editor of al-Dastour for trial for libelling Transport and Communications Minister Soleiman Metwalli.
